_comment: M16 curriculum spine. levels: id in levels.json + status. units: a level's sections. lessons: wired to M14 objects via `objectives`; `source` = steps:<catalog id> | view:alphabet | view:vocabulary | generate. A0 + A1 carry real lesson nodes; A2-C2 are unit stubs (the map) filled by M20+. Authored English copy only; no Arabic content added here.

units.title: The Arabic Alphabet
units.blurb: All 28 letters — name, sound, the four positional forms, and which six never join to the left.

units.title: Ḥarakāt & Reading Marks
units.blurb: The short vowels, sukūn, shaddah, tanwīn, and the long vowels — everything written above and below the line.

units.title: Building & Blending Syllables
units.blurb: Combine a consonant and a mark into a syllable, then read open, closed, and doubled syllables aloud.

units.title: First Words & Sounds
units.blurb: Your first real vocabulary, plus ear training and pronunciation practice on familiar words.

units.title: Your First Sentences
units.blurb: The nominal sentence, noun–adjective agreement, the definite article, and present-tense verbs for reading.

units.title: Reading Beyond Full Vowels
units.blurb: The same sentences with the vowel marks progressively removed — a first look at how Arabic is really written.

units.title: Everyday Words
units.blurb: High-frequency vocabulary for daily life — colours, useful questions, people, and describing things.

units.title: Talking About People & Places
units.blurb: Family, homes, towns, and the phrases that connect them. In development.

units.title: Numbers 1–10
units.blurb: Counting, the counted noun, and telling the time — the start of the numbers strand. In development.

units.title: The Verbal Sentence
units.blurb: Past and present tense of Form I, VSO word order, and كان. In development.

units.title: The Genitive Construct (Iḍāfa)
units.blurb: Noun-to-noun possession, the backbone of Arabic phrasing. In development.

units.title: Root & Pattern — First Look
units.blurb: How ك-ت-ب gives كِتَاب, كَاتِب, مَكْتَب — recognising word families. In development.

units.title: Numbers, Counting & Time
units.blurb: 11–99, gender polarity, dates, prices, and the clock. In development.

units.title: Reading Short Paragraphs
units.blurb: Fully-vowelled connected text on familiar topics; separating main idea from detail. In development.

units.title: Everyday Exchanges
units.blurb: Shopping, directions, and routine conversation — listening and speaking. In development.

units.title: Derived Verb Forms II–X
units.blurb: The ten forms, their meaning tendencies, and how to recognise them in text. In development.

units.title: Relative Clauses & Longer Sentences
units.blurb: الَّذِي and its family, إنّ وأخواتها, and joining ideas into paragraphs. In development.

units.title: Verbal Nouns & Participles
units.blurb: The maṣdar and active/passive participles — Arabic's engine for abstraction. In development.

units.title: Reading Unvowelled MSA
units.blurb: Supplying vowels from pattern and context on familiar-topic prose. In development.

units.title: Understanding Standard Speech
units.blurb: Short narratives, interviews, and factual reports at natural pace. In development.

units.title: Writing Connected Texts
units.blurb: Description, narrative, and informal messages with conjunctions and relative clauses. In development.

units.title: The Full Case System (Iʿrāb)
units.blurb: Nominative, accusative, and genitive used actively across nominal and verbal sentences. In development.

units.title: The Passive, the Jussive & Conditionals
units.blurb: Internal-vowel passive, the jussive after لم, and real and hypothetical conditions. In development.

units.title: Weak & Irregular Verbs
units.blurb: Assimilated, hollow, defective, doubled, and hamzated verbs — recognition and production. In development.

units.title: Reading the News
units.blurb: Unvowelled authentic articles and reports; following the argument and separating fact from comment. In development.

units.title: Broadcast & Extended Audio
units.blurb: News bulletins, documentaries, and discussion on concrete and abstract topics. In development.

units.title: Argumentative Writing
units.blurb: A paragraph that states a position, supports it, and concludes — with paragraphing and cohesion. In development.

units.title: Rhetorical Syntax & Style
units.blurb: Fronting, emphasis, particle nuance, and stylistic case variation. In development.

units.title: Editorials, Essays & Literary Prose
units.blurb: Register shifts, ellipsis, complex subordination, and implicit meaning. In development.

units.title: Register & Formal Correspondence
units.blurb: Choosing style for the reader; formal letters, reports, and structured essays. In development.

units.title: Following Lectures & Debates
units.blurb: Extended, loosely-structured speech; humour, irony, and speaker attitude. In development.

units.title: Fluent Discussion
units.blurb: Precise formulation, skilful turn-taking, and defending a point of view. In development.

units.title: Advanced Iʿrāb & Contested Parses
units.blurb: Stylistic and disputed parses; analysing syntactic ambiguity in real text. In development.

units.title: Classical & Heritage Texts
units.blurb: Pre-modern prose and poetry, with correct iʿrāb read aloud. In development.

units.title: Academic & Analytical Writing
units.blurb: Sustained argument, classical constructions, and deliberate stylistic variation. In development.

units.title: Near-Native Comprehension
units.blurb: Critical analysis of sophisticated texts for structure, assumption, and effect. In development.

units.title: Idiomatic & Stylistic Mastery
units.blurb: Colloquial-register fluency, rare and figurative vocabulary, near-native nuance. In development.

lessons.title: Meet the Arabic Alphabet
lessons.blurb: An overview of all 28 letters — their names and the sounds they make.

lessons.title: Arabic Letter Shapes
lessons.blurb: How each letter changes shape depending on its position in a word, and the six non-joiners.

lessons.title: Letter Writing Practice
lessons.blurb: Trace each letter to learn how it is drawn.

lessons.title: Directional Stroke-Order Writing
lessons.blurb: Watch, trace, then write each letter with the correct stroke order and direction.

lessons.title: Harakāt & Reading Marks
lessons.blurb: Every Arabic reading mark — short vowels, sukūn, shaddah, tanwīn, and long vowels — across the full alphabet.

lessons.title: Reading Foundations
lessons.blurb: Put letters, marks, and syllables together to read short, familiar Arabic aloud.

lessons.title: Reading Simple Syllables
lessons.blurb: Combine a consonant with each short vowel to read your first syllables.

lessons.title: Syllables: Long Vowels, Closed Syllables & Doubling
lessons.blurb: CVV, CVC, and geminated syllables — how Arabic builds and blends sound units.

lessons.title: First Arabic Words
lessons.blurb: Start building vocabulary with the core flashcard deck.

lessons.title: Listening Foundations
lessons.blurb: Hear, identify, and tell apart familiar Arabic words and phrases by ear.

lessons.title: Pronunciation Foundations
lessons.blurb: Listen, repeat aloud, and optionally record yourself on five familiar words.

lessons.title: Reading Real Sentences
lessons.blurb: Three fully-vowelled Arabic sentences — the nominal sentence and adjective agreement in action.

lessons.title: Grammar for Reading
lessons.blurb: Gender agreement, present-tense verb prefixes, and sun/moon assimilation of the definite article.

lessons.title: How Arabic Sentences Are Built
lessons.blurb: Singular / dual / plural, definite vs. indefinite, the verbless sentence, and negation with لَيْسَ.

lessons.title: This, That, My, In, On
lessons.blurb: Demonstratives هَذَا / هَذِهِ, the possessive endings, and the core prepositions with their genitive ending.

lessons.title: Reading Without Full Vowelling
lessons.blurb: The same sentences with the ḥarakāt progressively removed — reading Arabic as it is really written.

lessons.title: Colours
lessons.blurb: The core colour words, including the ones that follow the nisba (-iyy) pattern.

lessons.title: Useful Questions
lessons.blurb: Four everyday questions you can use right away.

lessons.title: He, She, They
lessons.blurb: The subject pronouns هُوَ, هِيَ, هُمْ — the ones you meet first in reading.

lessons.title: Describing Things
lessons.blurb: Easy and difficult, and other adjectives for talking about the world. In development.

lessons.title: Family & People
lessons.blurb: Child, boy, man, woman, uncle, aunt — and the word for "name".

lessons.title: Food & Meals
lessons.blurb: Juice, egg, cheese, salt, apple, the three meals, and how to say you are hungry.

lessons.title: Around the Home
lessons.blurb: Wall, floor, garden, and the word for "clean".

lessons.title: Telling the Time of Day
lessons.blurb: Hour, minute, day, noon, and the adverbs early / late / always / sometimes / before / after.

lessons.title: Everyday Actions
lessons.blurb: Twelve common verbs — come, sleep, wake up, study, live, want, play, open, close, sit, walk — plus "to have".

lessons.title: This, That & the Little Words
lessons.blurb: هَذَا / هَذِهِ / هَؤُلَاءِ, the core prepositions فِي عَلَى مِنْ إِلَى مَعَ, and لَيْسَ.
